definitions.gloss: candied dried baby sardines; another name for {田作|たづく}り
definitions.explanation: Small dried sardines roasted and coated in a sweet soy glaze, eaten at New Year. The same dish as {田作|たづく}り; ごまめ is the name used in western Japan and in older cookbooks.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧ごまめ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}っていた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother used to make gomame every year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{関東|かんとう}→関東：00186_kantou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{田作|たづく}り→田作り：30553_tazukuri⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ぶ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{関西|かんさい}→関西：00179_kansai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ごまめ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: In the Kanto region it is called tazukuri, but in Kansai it is usually called gomame.

notes:
Sometimes written {五万米|ごまめ} with characters chosen for their auspicious meaning rather than their sound value.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Dried sardines were once spread on rice paddies as fertilizer, which is why the dish is also called ⟦{田作|たづく}り→田作り：30553_tazukuri⟧ ("field-making"). Either way the dish is a wish for a good harvest, and it is one of the three celebratory dishes of ⟦{関東|かんとう}→関東：00186_kantou⟧-style ⟦おせち{料理|りょうり}→おせち料理：26981_osechiryouri⟧.
